text: After passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
As was his habit, Paul went in, and on three Sabbath days he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
explaining and showing that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead, saying, This Jesus I am telling you about is the Messiah.
Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few prominent women.

But the other Jews became jealous, and gathering some troublemakers from the marketplace, they formed a mob and set the whole city in an uproar, storming Jason's house looking for Paul and Silas to bring them out to the crowd.
When they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other believers before the city officials, shouting, These men who have caused trouble all over the world have now come here too,
and Jason has taken them into his home. They are all defying Caesar's decrees, saying there is another king called Jesus.
This news stirred up the crowd and the officials alike,
and after collecting bail money from Jason and the others, they let them go.
As soon as it was night, the believers sent Paul and Silas off to Berea, and on arriving they went into the Jewish synagogue.
The people there were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica, welcoming the message eagerly and studying the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true.
As a result many of them believed, along with a good number of prominent Greek women and men.
But when the Jews from Thessalonica found out Paul was preaching God's word in Berea too, they went there also, agitating the crowds and stirring up trouble.
The believers quickly sent Paul on toward the coast, while Silas and Timothy stayed behind.
Those escorting Paul brought him all the way to Athens, then went back with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as they could.
While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled to see the city so full of idols.
So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearing Gentiles, and every day in the marketplace with whoever happened to be there.

Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also debated with him. Some asked, What is this rambler trying to say? Others said, He seems to be promoting foreign gods, because he was preaching about Jesus and the resurrection.
So they took him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, Can you tell us about this new teaching you are presenting?
You are bringing us some strange ideas, and we want to know what they mean.
(All the Athenians and the foreigners living there spent their time doing nothing but talking about or listening to the newest ideas.)
Paul then stood up in the middle of the Areopagus and said, Men of Athens, I see that you are extremely religious in every way.
As I walked around looking at the things you worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: To an unknown god. So I am here to tell you about the very thing you worship without knowing it.
The God who made the world and everything in it, since he is Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by human hands,
and he isn't served by human hands as though he needed anything, because he is the one who gives everyone life, breath, and everything else.
From one man he made every nation of humanity to live across the whole earth, and he set the exact times and boundaries for where they would live,
so that they would search for God and perhaps reach out and find him, though he is not far from any of us.
For in him we live and move and exist, just as some of your own poets have said, We too are his offspring.
Since we are God's offspring, we shouldn't think the divine being is like an image of gold, silver, or stone, shaped by human skill and imagination.
God overlooked the times when people did not understand, but now he commands everyone everywhere to turn from sin,
because he has set a day when he will judge the world fairly through a man he has appointed, and he has given proof of this to everyone by raising that man from the dead.
When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some of them laughed it off, while others said, We would like to hear more from you about this some other time.
At that point Paul left the meeting.
But some people joined him and became believers, including Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus council, a woman named Damaris, and some others with them.
